# luma.gl

> WebGPU and WebGL2 framework documentation for visualization and compute.


## docs

luma gl is a high performance WebGL and WebGPU toolkit

- [Introduction](https://luma.gl/next/docs.md): luma gl is a high performance WebGL and WebGPU toolkit

### getting-started

Create a portable WebGPU and WebGL 2 triangle in a TypeScript application.

- [Getting started](https://luma.gl/next/docs/getting-started.md): Create a portable WebGPU and WebGL 2 triangle in a TypeScript application.

### capabilities

Detailed feature matrices for GPU-native dataframes, graph and raster analytics, large-scale visualization, WebGPU and WebGL2 rendering, ray tracing, shaders, and assets.

- [Visualization and compute, at GPU scale.](https://luma.gl/next/docs/capabilities.md): Detailed feature matrices for GPU-native dataframes, graph and raster analytics, large-scale visualization, WebGPU and WebGL2 rendering, ray tracing, shaders, and assets.

#### external-webgl-context

This guide shows how to connect luma.gl to a WebGL context that is created and owned by MapLibre GL JS. It uses the webgl2Adapter.attach API to wrap the map's context in a WebGLDevice and keep a WebGLCanvasContext synchronized with MapLibre's canvas.

- [External WebGL Contexts with MapLibre](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/external-webgl-context.md): This guide shows how to connect luma.gl to a WebGL context that is created and owned by MapLibre GL JS. It uses the webgl2Adapter.attach API to wrap the map's context in a WebGLDevice and keep a WebGLCanvasContext synchronized with MapLibre's canvas.

#### lighting

Add Phong shading to a textured cube using luma.gl's shader module system.

- [Lighting](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/lighting.md): Add Phong shading to a textured cube using luma.gl's shader module system.

#### shader-hooks

Shader hooks let shader modules inject code into designated points in a shader. This example defines an OFFSET_POSITION hook that two modules use to shift geometry left or right.

- [Shader Hooks](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/shader-hooks.md): Shader hooks let shader modules inject code into designated points in a shader. This example defines an OFFSET_POSITION hook that two modules use to shift geometry left or right.

#### shader-modules

This tutorial shows how to build reusable shader functionality with luma.gl's shader modules. The example below defines a custom color module that converts HSV to RGB and adds moving highlight bands to two different models.

- [Shader Modules](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/shader-modules.md): This tutorial shows how to build reusable shader functionality with luma.gl's shader modules. The example below defines a custom color module that converts HSV to RGB and adds moving highlight bands to two different models.

#### shader-plugins

ShaderPlugin packages reusable shader behavior that can be attached to a Model or Computation. This example renders a grid of triangles from one base shader pair. One plugin adds procedural fill patterns, while clipShaderPlugin adds portable whole-instance and per-fragment clipping.

- [Shader Plugins](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/shader-plugins.md): ShaderPlugin packages reusable shader behavior that can be attached to a Model or Computation. This example renders a grid of triangles from one base shader pair. One plugin adds procedural fill patterns, while clipShaderPlugin adds portable whole-instance and per-fragment clipping.

#### transform

This tutorial uses BufferTransform to update per-instance data on the GPU and render thousands of wandering triangles. The compute shader runs in a transform feedback pass before each draw.

- [Transform](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/transform.md): This tutorial uses BufferTransform to update per-instance data on the GPU and render thousands of wandering triangles. The compute shader runs in a transform feedback pass before each draw.

#### transform-feedback

This tutorial demonstrates animating geometry using transform feedback via the BufferTransform class. A compute shader rotates triangle vertices on the GPU each frame.

- [Transform Feedback](https://luma.gl/next/docs/tutorials/transform-feedback.md): This tutorial demonstrates animating geometry using transform feedback via the BufferTransform class. A compute shader rotates triangle vertices on the GPU each frame.

#### engine

Build rendered applications around Model, then add updates, redraw, interaction, scenegraphs, animation, compute, and passes only where needed.

- [Engine programming](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine.md): Build rendered applications around Model, then add updates, redraw, interaction, scenegraphs, animation, compute, and passes only where needed.
- [ANARI renderer architecture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/anari-architecture.md): Understand forward, deferred, and graph-based ray-tracing architecture, caching, and performance.
- [Build an ANARI scene](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/anari-first-scene.md): Create, commit, render, resize, animate, and inspect a retained ANARI scene.
- [ANARI JSON scenes](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/anari-json-scenes.md): Validate, author, generate, animate, and import declarative ANARI scene descriptions.
- [Declarative rendering with ANARI](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/anari-rendering.md): Choose and learn luma.gl's experimental retained ANARI scene workflow and renderers.
- [Animation and Deformation](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/animation.md): The @luma.gl/engine animation system plays reusable keyframe clips, blends overlapping actions, and applies morph-target deformation without depending on a particular asset format or renderer. glTF adapters, retained scenes, and custom applications can all use the same engine primitives.
- [Engine cookbook](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/cookbook.md): Each recipe assumes an existing Device. The snippets emphasize the object or update that changes;
- [Engine features](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features.md): Explore surface appearance and rendering capabilities through public APIs and live glTF samples.
- [Animated crowds and levels of detail](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/animated-crowds.md): Render independently animated characters with shared GPU geometry and select mesh detail by projected screen size.
- [Animation and deformation](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/animation.md): Animation combines clip playback, skeletal deformation, and morph targets to bring characters and scene objects to life.
- [Anisotropic reflection](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/anisotropy.md): Anisotropic reflection stretches highlights along a surface direction, useful for brushed metal and directional surface finishes.
- [Compressed geometry and textures](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/asset-compression.md): Compressed geometry and textures reduce asset transfer size and can reduce GPU texture storage when the device supports the resulting format.
- [Base color](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/base-color.md): Base color sets the diffuse color of a dielectric and the reflected color of a metal, combining a factor, a texture, and vertex colors.
- [Bump Mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/bump-mapping.md): Bump mapping derives small normal perturbations from a height texture without moving mesh vertices.
- [Clearcoat](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/clearcoat.md): Clearcoat adds a secondary glossy layer over a base surface, useful for varnish, lacquer, and automotive paint.
- [Diffuse transmission and scattering](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/diffuse-transmission.md): Diffuse transmission lets light emerge from the opposite side of a thin or scattering surface, useful for leaves, paper, and translucent ceramics.
- [Dispersion](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/dispersion.md): Dispersion separates transmitted wavelengths, producing colored fringes through refractive glass.
- [Double-sided surfaces](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/double-sided.md): Double-sided materials render both faces of thin surfaces and orient their shading normals for the visible face.
- [Emissive surfaces](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/emission.md): Emission makes a surface contribute its own visible radiance, including values above the display white level.
- [Emissive strength](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/emissive-strength.md): Emissive strength scales a surface’s emitted radiance beyond the core emissive color range for HDR highlights and bright displays.
- [Index of refraction](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/index-of-refraction.md): Index of refraction controls the optical contrast at a dielectric boundary and influences reflection and transmitted light.
- [Mesh instancing](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/instancing.md): Instancing draws many placements of shared geometry with one draw per compatible primitive instead of duplicating models.
- [Iridescence](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/iridescence.md): Thin-film interference produces view-dependent colors, useful for coated glass, soap films, and decorative finishes.
- [Punctual lighting](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/lighting.md): Directional, point, and spot lights provide explicit scene illumination with controllable direction, intensity, and color.
- [Lightmaps](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/lightmaps.md): Lightmaps add precomputed surface illumination to luma.gl materials. They are useful for static
- [Material variants](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/material-variants.md): Material variants switch authored surface appearances while preserving the scene hierarchy and model identities.
- [Metallic](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/metallic.md): Metallic controls the transition between a dielectric surface, such as plastic, and a conductor, such as bare metal.
- [Metallic and rough surfaces](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/metallic-roughness.md): Base color, metallic response, and roughness describe surfaces ranging from matte dielectrics to polished metals.
- [Normal mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/normal-mapping.md): A normal map changes the direction used for lighting to reveal fine surface detail while preserving the mesh silhouette.
- [Ambient occlusion](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/occlusion.md): An occlusion texture darkens creases and cavities using precomputed visibility, adding local surface shading without additional geometry.
- [Opacity and cutouts](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/opacity.md): Material alpha supports partially transparent surfaces and binary cutouts such as foliage, fences, and decals.
- [Roughness](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/roughness.md): Roughness controls the spread of microfacet reflections, from sharp polished highlights to broad matte reflections.
- [Sheen](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/sheen.md): Sheen adds a soft grazing-angle response for fabric, velvet, and other surfaces with fine fibers.
- [Specular reflection](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/specular.md): Specular reflection controls the strength and tint of dielectric highlights independently of the base diffuse color.
- [Normal and bump mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/surface-detail.md): Normal and height textures add apparent fine surface detail without increasing mesh tessellation.
- [Texture coordinates and transforms](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/texture-coordinates.md): Independent texture coordinate sets and transforms let each surface map use its own placement, rotation, and scale.
- [Thin-Wall Scattering](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/thin-wall-scattering.md): Thin-wall scattering divides transmitted light between specular transmission and diffuse
- [Transmission, volume, and dispersion](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/transmission.md): Transparent materials transmit light through a surface; thickness, absorption, and wavelength separation describe glass and colored volumes.
- [Unlit surfaces](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/unlit.md): Unlit surfaces preserve their surface color without evaluating scene lighting, useful for signs, diagrams, and baked artwork.
- [Scene visibility](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/visibility.md): Hide a scene subtree while preserving its hierarchy and resources for later reuse.
- [Volume absorption](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/volume.md): Volume thickness and absorption tint transmitted light according to the distance it travels through a material.
- [Volume Scattering](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/features/volume-scattering.md): Volume scattering approximates light redirected inside a material using local thickness and a directional phase response.
- [Interaction, picking, and highlighting](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/interactivity.md): Route browser input into camera controls or GPU picking, then use the selected identity to drive ordinary render-state highlighting.
- [Materials](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/materials.md): In luma.gl, a Material describes reusable surface state for one shading model
- [Redraw on demand](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/redraw.md): Treat Engine redraw flags as invalidation signals so static views stop rendering while updates and animation remain responsive.
- [Scenegraph Controllers and Deformation](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scene-controllers.md): Controllers operate on resolved scene objects. They do not require glTF source arrays,
- [Scenegraphs](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph.md): A luma.gl scene combines a hierarchy of spatial nodes with shared rendering resources
- [Spatial Audio](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-audio.md): AudioController attaches audio emitters and listener state to engine scene nodes. Its runtime
- [Scenegraph Billboards](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-billboards.md): BillboardController derives camera-facing draw transforms for selected scenegraph nodes.
- [Scenegraph Interactivity](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-interactivity.md): The engine's Interactivity runtime evaluates supported typed behavior graphs. Applications
- [Physical Joints](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-joints.md): A physical joint constrains the relative motion of two attachment frames. luma.gl's
- [Scenegraph Lights](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-lights.md): Scenegraph lighting attaches light definitions to spatial nodes. AreaLightController resolves
- [Morph Targets](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-morphs.md): Morph targets describe vertex-attribute deltas from a mesh's base geometry. luma.gl combines
- [Scenegraph Physics Integration](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-physics.md): The engine describes scene objects and constraint attachments. The graph physics
- [Skins and Skeletal Deformation](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/scenegraph-skins.md): A skin binds a mesh to an ordered set of scenegraph nodes. luma.gl's SkinController resolves
- [Shader Inputs](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/shader-inputs.md): ShaderInputs is the engine-side bridge between shader-module props and the
- [Choosing an Engine compute helper](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-guide/engine/transforms.md): Choose between WebGPU Computation, WebGL 2 BufferTransform, legacy texture transforms, direct Core passes, and GPU Core.

- [Ray tracing quality presets](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/ray-tracing-quality-presets.md): getRayTracingQualityPreset('interactive' | 'still') returns a fresh set of renderer
- [Ray-tracing renderer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/ray-tracing-renderer.md): This page describes the raytrace renderer selected by an ANARIFrame.
- [Structured volume ray marching](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/raymarch.md): Render scalar and vector fields from buffers or 3D textures with reusable WebGPU volume ray marching.
- [SceneRenderer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/scene-renderer.md): SceneRenderer renders retained, physically based surface descriptions on WebGPU and WebGL. It
- [SelectionOutline](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/selection-outline.md): SelectionOutline in @luma.gl/anari draws a WebGPU selection overlay from a
- [ShadowMapRenderer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/shadow-map-renderer.md): ShadowMapRenderer is an experimental WebGPU and WebGL2 light-space shadow system. It owns stable

- [WBOITRenderer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/anari/wboit-renderer.md): WBOITRenderer implements weighted blended order-independent transparency on WebGPU and WebGL2.

#### core

Create portable GPU resources, pipelines, passes, commands, and presentation contexts across WebGPU and WebGL 2.

- [Adapter](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/adapter.md): From v9.1
- [Bindings](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/bindings.md): Bindings are the GPU resources that shader code accesses through declared
- [BufferLayout](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/buffer-layout.md): The bufferLayout type provides information about how the application is planning to
- [CanvasContext](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/canvas-context.md): A CanvasContext connects a GPU Device to an HTMLCanvasElement or OffscreenCanvas.

- [DeviceFeatures](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/device-features.md): The luma.gl Device provides a device "feature" system that allows applications
- [DeviceInfo](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/device-info.md): The device.info field holds a small DeviceInfo object that provides information about the device, such as driver, GPU, shading language etc.
- [DeviceLimits](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/device-limits.md): The device.limits field contains limits object that indicates what the current platform supports.

- [GPU parameters](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/parameters.md): Pipeline parameters are fixed state; pass parameters describe a target and its mutable draw state.
- [PipelineFactory](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/pipeline-factory.md): PipelineFactory caches and reuses RenderPipeline and ComputePipeline instances for one device.
- [PresentationContext](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/presentation-context.md): From v9.3
- [Buffer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/buffer.md): Holds a block of GPU memory. The length of a buffer cannot be changed after creation.

- [CommandEncoder](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/command-encoder.md): A CommandEncoder records GPU commands that can later be sealed into a CommandBuffer and submitted to a Device.
- [ComputePass](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/compute-pass.md): WebGPU supported
- [ComputePipeline](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/compute-pipeline.md): WebGPU supported
- [ExternalTexture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/external-texture.md): WebGPU supported
- [Fence](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/fence.md): A GPU->CPU synchronization primitive that signals / resolves when any GPU commands submitted prior to the Fence have completed.
- [Framebuffer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/framebuffer.md): A Framebuffer groups color and optional depth/stencil texture views for a
- [PipelineLayout](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/pipeline-layout.md): PipelineLayout describes the binding groups available to a render or compute pipeline.
- [QuerySet](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/query-set.md): A QuerySet stores asynchronous GPU query results.

- [Resource](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/resource.md): Resource is the abstract base class for GPU objects created by a Device. It standardizes common fields such as identifiers and backend handles that are shared across buffers, textures, passes, and similar GPU resources.
- [Sampler](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/sampler.md): A Sampler is an immutable object that holds a set of sampling parameters for texture access.
- [Shader](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/shader.md): The Shader class holds a compiled shader.
- [Texture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/texture.md): A Texture is a GPU resource containing one or more images with a shared pixel format. Shaders may
- [TextureView](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/texture-view.md): A TextureView is a view onto some subset of the texture subresources defined by a particular Texture.
- [TransformFeedback](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/transform-feedback.md): WebGPU not supported
- [VertexArray](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/resources/vertex-array.md): A VertexArray stores a set of vertex attribute bindings, including the index buffer.
- [ShaderBlockLayout](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/core/shader-block-layout.md): ShaderBlockLayout is the portable description of how luma.gl packs uniform-style

#### engine

Render models with geometry and shader inputs, manage redraw and interaction, and compose animation, scenes, compute, and passes.

- [Engine](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine.md): Render models with geometry and shader inputs, manage redraw and interaction, and compose animation, scenes, compute, and passes.
- [AnimationLoop](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation-loop.md): AnimationLoop manages a render loop around a luma.gl Device.
- [AnimationLoopTemplate](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation-loop-template.md): AnimationLoopTemplate is a small abstract base class for applications that prefer a class-based render lifecycle on top of AnimationLoop.
- [AnimationMixer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation/animation-mixer.md): The AnimationMixer plays and blends reusable AnimationClip instances. A clip groups AnimationTrack objects, and each track updates an application property through an AnimationBinding. AnimationAction controls playback for an individual clip.
- [KeyFrames](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation/key-frames.md): Manages key frame animation data. Associates time points with arbitrary data and provides methods to access key times and data, and an interpolation factor, based on the current time.
- [Morph-Target Helpers](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation/morph-targets.md): @luma.gl/engine provides format-independent helpers for weighted vertex deformation. They combine morph-target deltas with immutable base geometry and can update an existing model's GPU vertex buffers in place.
- [Timeline](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/animation/timeline.md): Manages an animation timeline, with multiple channels that can be running at different rates, durations, etc. Many methods (play, pause) assume that the update method is being called once per frame with a "global time". This automatically done for AnimationLoop.timeline object.
- [BackgroundTextureModel](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/background-texture-model.md): BackgroundTextureModel is a specialized ClipSpace that renders one texture across the screen while preserving aspect ratio.
- [ClipSpace](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/clip-space.md): ClipSpace is a convenience subclass of Model that draws a fullscreen quad or oversized triangle in clip space.
- [BufferTransform](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/compute/buffer-transform.md): BufferTransform is the engine wrapper for WebGL transform-feedback workflows.
- [Computation](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/compute/computation.md): WebGPU supported
- [Swap](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/compute/swap.md): Swap is a small double-buffering helper for pairs of GPU resources.
- [TextureTransform](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/compute/texture-transform.md): TextureTransform is the engine helper for texture-to-texture transform passes.
- [DynamicBuffer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/dynamic-buffer.md): This resource convenience is now documented under Core dynamic resources. The engine compatibility export remains available.
- [DynamicTexture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/dynamic-texture.md): This resource convenience is now documented under Core dynamic resources. The engine compatibility export remains available.
- [Experimental Engine utilities](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental.md): These opt-in subpaths expose evolving utilities without adding them to the Engine root API.
- [ComparisonSplitter](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/comparison-splitter.md): ComparisonSplitter provides a reusable, accessible divider for comparing two views of the same
- [Glass Material](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/glass-material.md): glassMaterial is an experimental cross-backend shader module for refractive translucent surfaces.
- [Reflective Material](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/reflective-material.md): reflectiveMaterial is a lightweight cross-backend shader module for glossy surfaces. It combines
- [Experimental WebXR](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/webxr.md): From v10
- [WebXRCameraTexture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/webxr/webxr-camera-texture.md): From v10
- [WebXRManager](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/experimental/webxr/webxr-manager.md): From v10
- [Geometry](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/geometry.md): Geometry is a compatibility adapter over the CPU-side container from @math.gl/geometry.
- [Built-in Geometries](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/geometry/geometries.md): @luma.gl/engine exports several ready-made geometry classes. All of them extend Geometry and populate standard glTF mesh attribute semantics such as POSITION, NORMAL, and TEXCOORD_0.
- [GPUGeometry](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/geometry/gpu-geometry.md): GPUGeometry is the GPU-backed counterpart to Geometry.
- [makeStrokeGeometry](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/geometry/stroke-geometry.md): Triangulates a connected path into a local XY stroke, with butt, square, or round caps and miter, bevel, or round joins. Optional vertex elevations are preserved. Width and distance use the same units as the input coordinates; convert geographic coordinates to a local Cartesian system before calling this helper.
- [loadImageBitmap](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/load-image-bitmap.md): A simple small utility to load images from URLs. The loaded ImageBitmaps can be used to create textures.
- [Model](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/model.md): Model is the main engine-level rendering class in luma.gl.
- [OrbitControls](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/orbit-controls.md): OrbitControls adds pointer-driven orbiting, optional two-finger camera roll, wheel and pinch zoom, optional panning, automatic orbiting, and configurable camera bounds to an HTML canvas. The controls maintain a camera position and up direction around a target without depending on a specific renderer, scene graph, or GPU backend.
- [ShaderPassRenderer](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/passes/shader-pass-renderer.md): ShaderPassRenderer applies one or more ShaderPass or CompositeShaderPass definitions to a source texture and either renders the result back to a texture or draws it to the screen.
- [PhysicsController](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/physics-controller.md): Application-facing GPU physics for an existing engine scenegraph. Import from
- [PickingManager](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/picking-manager.md): PickingManager manages an offscreen picking framebuffer and the shader-input updates needed for luma.gl's engine picking modules.
- [GroupNode](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/scenegraph/group-node.md): GroupNode extends ScenegraphNode with child-node management and traversal helpers.
- [ModelNode](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/scenegraph/model-node.md): ModelNode extends ScenegraphNode with a Model and optional bounds / managed resources.
- [ScenegraphNode](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/scenegraph/scenegraph-node.md): ScenegraphNode is the base class for engine scenegraph objects.
- [ShaderInputs](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/shader-inputs.md): ShaderInputs stores per-module uniform values and binding values for shader modules.
- [TableTransform](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/tables/table-transform.md): TableTransform executes WebGL transform feedback over GPU table batches. It consumes a
- [@luma.gl/engine/text](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/text.md): Install @luma.gl/engine to use these optional subpaths. Text APIs are not exported from the
- [@luma.gl/engine/text-3d](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/text-3d.md): 3D text geometry helpers are exposed from the dedicated @luma.gl/engine/text-3d entry point.
- [VideoTexture](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/engine/video-texture.md): From v9.4

- [glTF area-light mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-area-lights.md): parseGLTFAreaLights() from @luma.gl/engine/gltf converts source size/aspect values into width/height bindings for the engine AreaLightController. See Scenegraph lights for the engine APIs.
- [glTF audio mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-audio.md): parseGLTFAudio() from @luma.gl/engine/gltf resolves emitters, source resources, graph routing, and environments into props for the engine AudioController. See Spatial audio for the engine APIs.
- [Audio environment profile](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-audio-environment.md): AudioController reads an initial profile of the KHRaudioenvironment draft. This is partial support, not full draft conformance.
- [glTF billboard mapping](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-billboard.md): parseGLTFBillboards() from @luma.gl/engine/gltf resolves draft billboard attachments into props for the engine BillboardController. See Scenegraph billboards for the engine APIs.
- [GPU-animated crowd API](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-crowd-api.md): Crowd boundaries, ownership, cleanup, diagnostics, and public API contracts.
- [GPU-animated crowd performance and LOD](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-crowd-performance.md): Joint-palette costs, screen-space levels of detail, vertex budgets, and decimation.
- [GPU-animated crowd usage](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-crowd-usage.md): Create, render, batch, and independently animate large glTF crowds.

- [glTF Asset Interchange](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-interchange.md): Asset export is application code. The shared example helper

- [KHR_materials_scatter](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/gltf/gltf-materials-scatter.md): The pinned draft has an initial thin-wall rendering profile in the canonical PBR material shaders on WebGL2 and WebGPU.

- [dggs](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/dggs.md): The dggs shader module provides WGSL helpers for compact 64-bit DGGS cell IDs
- [dirlight](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/dirlight.md): The dirlight shader module is a lightweight alternative to the full
- [colors, floatColors, and storageColors](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/float-colors.md): The colors shader module provides shared utilities for semantic colors in shader code.
- [fp32 (32-bit Floating Point)](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/fp32.md): Provides "improved" 32-bit math support to GPU shaders on certain platforms,
- [fp64 (Extended-Precision Shader Math)](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/fp64.md): luma.gl emulates extended precision by representing one scalar as two f32 values,
- [fp64arithmetic](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/fp64-arithmetic.md): The fp64arithmetic shader module provides the low-level double-single
- [gouraudMaterial](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/gouraud-material.md): The gouraudMaterial shader module provides functions to apply Gouraud shading
- [GPU picking](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/gpu-picking.md): GPU picking renders object identities into an offscreen framebuffer, then reads the identity
- [lambertMaterial](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/lambert-material.md): This lambertMaterial shader module provides a diffuse-only matte material
- [lighting](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/lighting.md): The lighting shader module collects scene lighting into a single uniform block
- [pathDash](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/path-dash.md): pathDash computes filtered dash coverage from cumulative path distance. It provides matching GLSL and WGSL fragment-stage implementations, with no textures or vertex-buffer allocation.
- [patternFill](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/pattern-fill.md): patternFill returns antialiased coverage for hatch, crosshatch, and dot fills. It supports GLSL
- [pbrMaterial](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/pbr-material.md): Implements luma.gl's shared physically based microfacet surface shading. Materials can be
- [phongMaterial](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/phong-material.md): This phongMaterial shader module provides functions to apply Phong shading
- [picking](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/picking.md): Deprecated in v9.1
- [pointGlow](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/point-glow.md): pointGlow produces linear RGB radiance for a bounded point sprite with a white core and a
- [projection](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/project.md): The internal projection shader module shares view and projection matrices across GLSL shaders.
- [random](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/random.md): The random shader module injects a small random-number helper into shaders.
- [sketchStroke](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/sketch-stroke.md): Reusable GLSL and WGSL fragment coverage for solid or pencil-like strokes. Import sketchStroke
- [skin](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-modules/skin.md): The skin shader module provides GPU skinning helpers for skinned meshes,
- [ShaderPass](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-pass.md): ShaderPass is a ShaderModule
- [Bloom](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-passes/bloom.md): Spread bright scene highlights into a controllable photographic glow. luma.gl provides a compact
- [Brightness and Contrast](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-passes/brightness-contrast.md): Shape overall exposure and tonal separation with a compact, single-pass color adjustment. Use

- [Camera-Reprojection Antialiasing](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-passes/camera-reprojection-antialiasing.md): Reconstruct previous-frame image coordinates from scene depth and camera transforms when a

- [Depth of Field](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-passes/depth-of-field.md): Keep a selected camera-space distance sharp while softening nearer and farther geometry.

- [HDR Auto Exposure](https://luma.gl/next/docs/api-reference/shaders/shader-passes/hdr-auto-exposure.md): Continuously meter scene luminance and adapt camera exposure entirely on the GPU.
